..
Issued at 140 PM EDT Sun Oct 11 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast:

Remnants of what was once tropical cyclone "Isaias" well to our 
southeast...rotating up into the mid-Atlantic states. Broad upper 
level ridging extending north of these remnants, centering itself 
across the western Great Lakes. Perfect recipe for unseasonably warm 
conditions continues across the Northwoods...with overhead deep 
layer return flow between departing surface high and slow southeast 
dropping cold front just entering northern Lake Superior. Overhead 
airmass already a warm one, and when combined with those southerly 
winds and plenty of sunshine has again propelled temperatures well 
up into the 70s across most of our area. May even see an isolated 
location or two hit 80 yet this afternoon. While not record setting, 
these readings are still well above normal as we head into the 
middle of October.

Overhead ridging slowly gets knocked down heading into this week as 
northern stream flow becomes a bit more suppressed. This will drive 
that upstream cold front southeast, slowly crossing our area Monday 
through Tuesday morning. This front will bring some much needed rain 
chances and the return to more normal temperatures. Potential for a 
much stronger northern stream wave to arrive later this week, 
perhaps bringing a shot of even cooler air along with it. 

Primary Forecast Concerns:

Temperature trends through the period and shower evolution with that 
passing front to kick off this work week.

Details: 

Mild and dry weather tonight sets the stage for more unseasonably 
warm weather on Monday. That weak front does begin to drop across 
eastern upper during the morning...likely extending across northern 
lower Michigan during the afternoon. Still plenty of time for an 
excellent diurnal temperature response across northern lower 
Michigan within the pre-frontal southwest flow environment. Thermal 
progs easily support highs well up into the 70s for most south of 
the big bridge, with readings pushing 80 easily attainable... 
especially down near Saginaw Bay. Again, short of records, but a 
good 10 to 20 degrees above normal. Post-frontal east winds, more 
clouds, and even the threat for a few light showers will keep those 
across eastern upper a touch cooler, but still looking at highs up 
into the 60s.

Weather turns a bit more active Monday night into Tuesday morning as 
that front continues to work slowly south. Moisture increases 
substantially, to include even some remnants of current tropical 
system rotating up into the southwest Conus. Passing weak low along 
this front and some entrance region upper jet dynamics will help 
work over this increasing moisture, driving increasing chances for 
some much needed rain. Current juxtaposition of better deep layer 
forcing and moisture suggest most organized showers will be found 
across eastern upper and areas north of M-32 in northern lower later 
Monday night into Tuesday morning...with more scattered activity to 
the south. Just enough elevated instability to perhaps support a few 
embedded thunderstorms as well, but definitely nothing too intense 
expected. Not looking at any real significant rains, with most areas 
likely receiving well under a half an inch by later Tuesday morning. 
Of course, isolated heavier totals remain possible, especially where 
embedded deeper convection occurs.

Front looks to clear our area by later Tuesday, taking any shower 
threat along with it. While not nearly as warm as the past few days, 
still looking at relatively mild conditions Tuesday. Northwest winds 
usher in a considerably cooler airmass by Wednesday, with highs 
mostly in the upper 50s to lower 60s. Still looking at northern 
stream amplification to occur later this week, driving deepening 
troughing into or perhaps just east of the area Thursday night into 
Friday. Still considerable uncertainty on just how aggressive this 
trough deepening will be across the Great Lakes...raising questions 
on just how much cold air we can tap. If some of the more aggressive 
scenarios are realized, could easily see falling temperatures into 
the 40s on Friday, with highs in the 40s to lower 50s on Saturday. 
Chances for showers will accompany this wave, with perhaps even some 
lake moisture contribution to those showers later Friday into Friday 
night. Temperatures look to begin to rebound some by Sunday as core 
of coldest temperature anomalies rotate off to the east.
